title: THE BOTTLE
note: FILE 01 from the script DRAFT 2 (owner, 4.11.2026; not yet approved). Each beat's `camera` is the script's own camera direction, rendered by `move`, `transition` and the camera-life effects. Narrated beats carry `say`; their length comes from the narrator's voice (produce.py) — `dur` is only the estimate for a dry run. `cont` beats carry the previous line on another panel, sharing its time by `share`. `t0: "word"` lands an effect on the word in `smash_at_word` (`word2` on `smash2_at_word`); `freeze: "word"` stops the camera there. `@CH1` is the character sheet in the red training top, measured on each run (roles.py, owner: green = Casillas = CH2). P05 = the keeper standing in the floodlights, P15 = entering the stadium at night (owner). Chapter 3's dossier is the desk; P18 (pile-on) is not uploaded, so the shoot-out line is held. The follow line (rule 136) and the closing line are added by produce.py through studio/script.py with_cta.

beats.say: May, two thousand and two. The World Cup in Korea and Japan is sixteen days away. Spain's first game: Slovenia, in Gwangju.
beats.camera: top-down, slow crane down onto the folder; desk lamp flickers on

beats.say: Spain's number one is ready. Thirty-two, the best season of his life behind him.
beats.camera: CH1 sheet pinned in the open folder · push-in, red string slides to it

beats.say: Friday evening, a hotel near Jerez. He walks into the bathroom.
beats.camera: slow push-in down the corridor, the door swings

beats.say: A shelf. A heavy glass bottle of cologne.
beats.camera: macro push-in on the hand, depth blur rising

beats.say: He had spent his life catching things.
beats.camera: slow motion, 3D tilt as the bottle falls past camera, droplets drift

beats.say: This one got away.
beats.camera: whip-pan down, impact shake, white flash frame
hard cut, the stamp slams, ink bleeds

beats.say: His name: Santiago Cañizares, the goalkeeper of Valencia, champions of Spain. The shirt with the number one was his.
beats.camera: pull-out from the gloves to the whole goal

beats.say: Behind him, on the list, a kid from Real Madrid. Iker Casillas, about to turn twenty-one, had spent the spring on the bench.
beats.camera: page-slide reveal (S03 → P05), then a crane up the floodlight

beats.say: Then, on the fifteenth of May in Glasgow, the Champions League final. Real Madrid's goalkeeper César went down injured. The kid came on, and made the saves that kept a two-one lead.
beats.camera: push-in on the young keeper

beats.say: Two days later, Spain's camp near Jerez. Bags unpacked. Toiletries out. Back to that Friday evening.
beats.camera: slow orbit around the bottle on the shelf, light glints

beats.say: What happened next has two versions, and this file keeps both.
beats.camera: handheld drift, the light dims

beats.say: The one the wire services sent round the world that night: he knocked the bottle, it broke against the washbasin, and a shard of glass fell onto his right foot.
beats.camera: split-screen slide, version A on the left

beats.say: The one he told the next day, back from hospital at three in the morning: he had showered, reached for the cologne, it slipped — and he put out his foot to stop it. Like a ball.
beats.camera: rewind tape, replay faster, version B on the right

beats.say: Either way, the result was the same. The glass cut the tendon of his big toe.
beats.camera: crash zoom

beats.say: Surgery that night at the general hospital in Jerez: the tendon that lifts the big toe of his right foot, cut clean through. No World Cup.
beats.camera: long dolly down the corridor with the trolley

beats.say: In front of the cameras he refused to call himself unlucky. From the start of his career, he said, he had had more than his share of good luck.
beats.camera: camera flashes, slow push-in

fx.label: PARAPHRASED · NOT A QUOTE
fx.text: Cañizares to the press, in our words

beats.say: And the coach, José Antonio Camacho, had a hole in his team two weeks before the opening game.
beats.camera: static, the TV glow pulses

beats.say: César was still injured from Glasgow, so he could not step in. The gloves went to the kid.
beats.camera: top-down, the folder flips open (the dossier desk: the kid’s file)

beats.say: Sixteenth of June. Suwon, South Korea. A place in the quarter-finals against Ireland. Nearly thirty-nine thousand inside.
beats.camera: follow from behind through the tunnel, the bowl opens up

beats.say: Spain led, then Ireland won a penalty. Ian Harte struck it. Casillas went the right way. Kilbane put the rebound wide.
beats.camera: slow motion along the dive, freeze, burst

beats.say: Robbie Keane equalised in the ninetieth minute, and extra time settled nothing. The first penalty shoot-out of that World Cup.
beats.camera: slow pan along the line of players

beats.say: Matt Holland hit the bar. Casillas saved from David Connolly. He saved from Kevin Kilbane. Gaizka Mendieta scored. Spain through, three-two.
beats.camera: two quick whips, a hold on the last save

beats.say: Three penalties saved in one night, by a goalkeeper who should have been on the bench. Spain had a new saint: San Iker.
beats.camera: P17 held, confetti overlay · crane up and away
beats.fallback_for: P18 pile-on (not uploaded: the shoot-out line is held)

beats.say: In Madrid the next morning, it was his face on the front pages. The number one would be his for most of the next fifteen years.
beats.camera: pan along the newspapers

beats.say: Somewhere in a hotel near Jerez, there's a shelf where a bottle of cologne used to stand. It changed who played in goal for Spain. File closed.
beats.camera: slow pull-out to black

The Cologne Bottle That Cost a Goalkeeper the World Cup
The Bottle That Gave Spain a Saint
package.hook: Friday, 17 May 2002. Two weeks before the World Cup, Spain's number one goalkeeper, Santiago Cañizares, dropped a bottle of cologne in his hotel bathroom near Jerez. CLASSIFIED · FILE 01: what happened that night, in both the versions it is told, and how a twenty-year-old from Real Madrid ended up saving three penalties in one night in Suwon.

shorts.hook: A goalkeeper. A bottle of cologne. And gravity.
The kid who should have been on the bench
